findings.body: The SHA256 identity computation and subsequent reflection/type-resolution work runs on every call when `-UseNativeStructuralConversion` is set. Since the template is constant, consider caching (at script scope) the computed identity, resolved `[type]`, and any reflected members used for verification/invocation so hot-path Markdown parsing avoids repeated hashing/reflection overhead while preserving the same correctness checks.

This npm-environment sanitization block appears multiple times in the workflow (e.g., in the verification, install, and dependency-tree steps). Duplicating this logic increases the chance of future drift (one step updated while others aren’t). Consider moving the sanitization into a single repo-owned helper script (bash) that each step calls, or using a single step that exports the sanitized env values and a reusable command wrapper, so policy changes stay consistent across all npm invocations.
